answer: Every account is a vertex in an attestation graph, and nobody enters alone. A new identity answers a seeded challenge; five established jurors outside its co-attestation cluster then review the text, each staking 1,000 POA and forfeiting the bond if they approve a clone. Kin accounts attest each other in tight loops, and that umber smudge shows in one graph query. Forging 10,000 sybils takes 10,000 kin-free jurors who each risk a slashed bond, so the attack costs more than it earns. It grinds like a glacier: every loose stone ends flat.
